
VALIDATE-SPEC-ALIGNMENT
Check that a work unit has scenarios tagged with its ID

WHEN TO USE
  Use in the validating phase to confirm the work unit's scenarios are tagged with its ID before moving it to done.

PREREQUISITES
  • The work unit must exist in spec/work-units.json
  • Feature files live in spec/features/

USAGE
  fspec validate-spec-alignment <workUnitId> [options]

ARGUMENTS
  <workUnitId> (required)
    Work unit whose scenarios are checked (scenarios tagged @<workUnitId>)

OPTIONS
  --fix
    Accepted for compatibility; makes no changes

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Check before moving to done
    Example: # Check that the work unit has tagged scenarios
fspec validate-spec-alignment AUTH-001

# Check its coverage mappings
fspec audit --feature user-authentication --area coverage

# Move to done
fspec update-work-unit-status AUTH-001 done


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. Complete implementation → 2. Link coverage: fspec link-coverage <feature> → 3. Check tags: fspec validate-spec-alignment <workUnitId> → 4. Move to done: fspec update-work-unit-status <workUnitId> done

EXAMPLES
  1. Check that AUTH-001 has tagged scenarios
  $ fspec validate-spec-alignment AUTH-001
  ✓ All specs are aligned with tests and implementation

  2. A work unit without tagged scenarios
  $ fspec validate-spec-alignment DASH-002
    - No scenarios for DASH-002 (exit code 1)

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Failed to validate spec alignment: Work unit AUTH-999 not found
    Fix: Check the work unit ID: fspec list-work-units

  ✗ No scenarios for AUTH-001
    Fix: Tag the work unit's scenarios: fspec add-tag-to-scenario <feature> "<scenario>" @AUTH-001

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec validate
  fspec link-coverage
  fspec show-coverage
  fspec audit
  fspec update-work-unit-status

NOTES
  • A scenario counts when the line before its Scenario: line carries @<workUnitId>
  • Exits 1 and prints the warning when the work unit has no tagged scenarios
  • Use fspec audit --area coverage to check a feature's test and implementation mappings
